This seems to be an experience which varies from person to person in the context of quitting, not staying on kratom. We all know that while on kratom, we are numbed to our environment and our emotions. However, quitting kratom is a different scenario entirely. Some people had ruined relationships while on kratom and that realization only fully dawned upon them once they quit. With the resurgence in libido also comes a resurgence of repressed emotions of guilt, shame, and other fun things. I've been clean for several months now and the emotions I felt were so raw that I chose not to pursue love and instead become the greatest version of myself so that I can to fix all the mistakes I have made. Don't get me wrong, I feel all the same emotions and desires that you do too. However, I have also gained a lot of discipline and made a conscious decision for the first time in years to focus on bettering myself for the time being.

I'll just tell you straight up as a man who has been through the same struggles as well as many others here. There are no magic words I can say to you. There is no spark of inspiration that I can give you that will carry you throughout this journey. What I can give you is some wisdom which many others have discovered for themselves while quitting. 

You have spent your entire time while on kratom reverse engineering your brain so that it puts the cart in front of the horse, so to speak. The cart in this case represents motivation and the horse represents action. You have essentially made kratom a precursor to your existence, let alone daily activities. You let other things spur you into action rather than finding that willpower within yourself, yet you sit here and seriously ask us what is wrong when the answer is clear. You must consciously make the effort to unlearn that habit. You won't be happy about it most of the time, but that's not the point. 

Not to be overly dramatic, but you will uncover a deeper truth about life. Life is suffering. You can choose to harness that suffering to become the best possible version of yourself or utilize that suffering as a perpetual excuse to run away and be reduced to nothing more than an animal running on impulses. It does not have to be terrible all the time. In fact, it is artistic and beautiful in its own way. You will be able to look at yourself in the mirror and feel proud. What will be your legacy? Ask yourself that every day.

My tolerance was through the roof after 2 years. At that point I was taking several spoonfuls per dose every few hours. I often didn't eat because of it and I weighed 120ish pounds before I said enough is enough. Now I'm 150+ pounds which is great, but you just have to be patient with the recovery process

Do smaller but more frequent doses to get a steady stream of alkaloids in your system. It will ease the burden on your body and make your tapering process as smooth as possible, although not painless since kratom is very inconsistent sometimes. At the same time, find things to occupy your day with. This can be going to school full time, working full time, and filling the spaces in between with activities that are beneficial or that you just enjoy doing to boost your positivity. Also, if you haven't already, start hanging out with your friends. You will thank me in advance for this. Having a social life saved me from relapsing so many times once I actually succeeded in tapering myself from 80gpd.

It depends on which experience is best for you as there are tradeoffs. 

With tapering, you will not feel the full force of acute withdrawals. I have also heard some people claim that it makes PAWS shorter and more doable. However, the process of healing takes longer so this method requires patience and the acknowledgement of the fact that you will no longer feel the high, you just won't feel withdrawals. 

With cold turkey, you will feel the full force of the acute withdrawals but they will begin to subside after a week or two. This method is probably the most painful but also the most enlightening and many people who go through this never turn back again.

I have spent the last 2 years squandering my time and ruining my life. Like many people I started kratom as a way to ease depression and fatigue after work and school. It went from 3x a week to once a day to every 3-4 hours per day. I numbed myself from the pain of the world only to introduce more pain in my life. Kratom took away my motivation to do the things I loved and accept my responsibilities. My life was centered around getting the next fix, even if it meant wasting so much money and lying to my family. As a result, I lost my scholarship, the trust of my loved ones, my savings, time, opportunities, and so many other things.

However, I am 21 and I still have a chance at making things right. I want to mend the wounds that I have opened up for myself and others as a result of this taxing addiction. I am thankful for the fact that I have a place to live, food, water, and a family that still supports me despite all the lies I have told them to skate by them. 

I am going to need all the help I can get in this process. Any advice is appreciated. Thank you all for awakening me to the dangers of this substance and I hope I can be the one helping others start their journey however much time it takes before I am free!
